In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aging in Japan was deflationary, but the effects of aging on inflation are not always negative.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the aging of the population is deflationary, while the decline in birth rate is inflationary.
aging and the associated demographic transition are not a burden on future generation, but rather a burden on the current generation.
aging is a deflationary force in the long run, but not in the short run.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aging is a deflationary phenomenon in the long run, and the effect of aging on inflation should not be confused with that of the fiscal policy.
the aging population is not necessarily a threat to the sustainability of government debt.
the effects of fiscal policy on the price level should be evaluated in a dynamic setting that takes into account the political influence of different generations.
